title: Crispy Turmeric Rice Pancake with Prawns and Pork
summary: A Vietnamese-style banh xeo inspired pancake with a lacy, crisp turmeric batter, savoury pork and prawns, and fresh herbs on the side. Best eaten hot and folded into lettuce leaves with a tangy dipping sauce.
steps: Make the batter by whisking together the plain flour, cornstarch, turmeric, salt, vegetable stock and milk until smooth. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Mix the lime juice, sugar, garlic, chilli and a pinch of salt in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Add a splash of water if you want a lighter dipping sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add a quarter of the onion and cook for 1 minute until starting to soften.
Add a quarter of the pork and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until no longer pink. Add a quarter of the prawns and cook just until they turn pink. Remove to a plate and repeat with the remaining filling.

Wipe the pan if needed, then add a little oil and pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling quickly to cover the base. Scatter over some bean sprouts and spring onion, then spoon some of the pork and prawn filling over one half.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the underside is deep golden and crisp and the edges lift easily. Fold the pancake in half and slide onto a warm plate. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve immediately with lettuce, mint and coriander, and let everyone wrap pieces of pancake in the leaves with the dipping sauce.
